verdicts.evidence: modules/math/src/Plane.cpp (Plane::Transform(const Plane&, const Matrix&, Plane&)) calls Matrix::Transpose(transformedMatrix, transformedMatrix); modules/math/src/Matrix.cpp (Matrix::Transpose(const Matrix&, Matrix&)) writes M12..M14 before reading them back as M21..M41, so the aliased call symmetrises from the lower triangle. Re-derived both worked examples by hand from Vector4::Transform (row-vector product, modules/math/src/Vector4.cpp): translation (1,0,0) on plane y=1 gives (1,1,0,-1); RotationZ(PiOver2) on y=2 gives normal (1,0,0). XNA 4.0 IL (Microsoft.Xna.Framework Plane::Transform) inverts and reads rows of the inverse directly (x' = x*inv.M11 + y*inv.M12 + z*inv.M13 + d*inv.M14): aliasing-free. verdicts.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingBox.cpp (BoundingBox::Contains(const BoundingFrustum&)): first loop breaks at the first Disjoint corner; i==8 -> Contains, i!=0 -> Intersects, i==0 -> second loop over corners 1..7 returns Intersects on the first non-Contains corner else Contains. modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp: Contains(Vector3) returns Intersects for sqDistance == sqRadius; Contains(BoundingSphere) tests sqDistance <= (Radius - sphere.Radius)^2 (sign lost). XNA 4.0 IL: Contains(Vector3) -> Contains iff DistanceSquared < Radius*Radius else Disjoint; Contains(BoundingSphere) -> Disjoint unless R+r >= d, Contains iff R-r >= d, else Intersects. Both divergences hold; BoundingSphereTests.cpp ContainsPointOnBoundaryIsIntersects pins the CNA answer. Text error: the 'actual' sentence presents BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingBox) treating a corner on the surface as inside as part of the divergence, but XNA 4.0 IL (BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingBox)) reports Intersects only when a corner's LengthSquared > Radius*Radius, so it also counts a surface corner as inside; the same holds for Contains(BoundingFrustum)'s corner test. That overload's answer does not differ from XNA because of the surface rule.

corrections.actual: {{src:modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp|BoundingSphere.cpp}} returns Intersects for sqDistance == sqRadius in the point overload, where XNA 4.0 answers Disjoint (it returns Contains only for DistanceSquared < Radius*Radius). The sphere overload's Contains test is sqDistance <= (Radius - sphere.Radius) * (Radius - sphere.Radius): squaring discards the sign, so a radius-1 sphere asked about a concentric radius-5 sphere answers Contains. BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingBox) and Contains(const BoundingFrustum&) use the point overload only as a “corner is not Disjoint” test, which counts a corner lying exactly on the surface as inside; XNA's own corner test (outside only when the squared distance exceeds Radius*Radius) does the same, so the surface difference does not change those two overloads' answers.

verdicts.note: Divergences for the point and sphere overloads are real; only the box-overload remark was mis-attributed as a divergence.

Read: modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp (DirectX9Renderer::CreateEffectRenderer; no SupportsCapability, GetShaderDialectEXT or ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT override); modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp (custom-effect flush binds D3D9EffectRenderer); modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9EffectDraw.cpp (DirectX9Renderer::DrawPrimitivesExImpl, DrawBasicEffectEXT); modules/graphics/src/Xna/ShaderEffect.cpp (FillGpuDrawParams sets only customEffectRequested/customEffectRenderer); IGraphicsRenderer.hpp (GpuDrawParams defaults vertexColorEnabled=true, textureEnabled=false, lightingEnabled=false; ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT doc); GraphicsDevice.cpp (BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT). Two parts of the entry are overstated. (1) The expected contract is not CNA's: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT defines CustomEffects as 'a ShaderEffect object is accepted; source execution is a separate feature', and IGraphicsRenderer::ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT documents accepting the object while rendering with a fixed path as legitimate when the renderer answers false (the SOFTWARE/HEADLESS case). DIRECTX9 answers false and the profile tells callers source does not determine pixels, so 'CustomEffects reports true' is not a lying flag and the 3D fixed path is inside the documented contract. (2) 'silently ... no error' holds only for 16-byte VertexPositionColor streams: with the defaults a ShaderEffect leaves in GpuDrawParams the cascade reaches DrawBasicEffectEXT, which draws stride 16 with the stock vertex-colour shader and throws std::runtime_error ('(BasicEffect): stride N ... has no matching CNA vertex layout') for strides 20/24/32 and custom layouts. What survives: an inconsistent, misleadingly-named refusal for 3D, and an ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT()=false answer that under-claims the SpriteBatch route (plans/plan_dx9.md D9-112 scoped DIRECTX9 ShaderEffect to SpriteBatch::Begin(effect)). Low severity.

corrections.title: DIRECTX9 ignores a ShaderEffect on 3D draws (stock BasicEffect draw or a misleading vertex-layout error) and reports ShaderEffect source execution as false although its SpriteBatch executes it
corrections.summary: DIRECTX9 compiles ShaderEffect HLSL and runs it for SpriteBatch, but its 3D dispatch never reads the custom effect, so a 3D ShaderEffect draw is drawn with the stock vertex-colour BasicEffect shader (16-byte vertices) or fails with a BasicEffect vertex-layout runtime_error, while ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() answers false for both routes.
corrections.expected: CNA separates two answers. GraphicsCapability::CustomEffects states only that a ShaderEffect object is accepted (GraphicsDevice::BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT: “source execution is a separate feature”), and IGraphicsRenderer::ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() states whether the source text determines pixels; a renderer that accepts the object but draws with a fixed path is legitimate when it answers false, as SOFTWARE and HEADLESS do. Within that contract the answer should describe what the renderer's routes actually do, and a route that cannot run the custom program should either use a fixed path consistently or refuse by name. DIRECTX11 and DIRECTX12 run the source on every route and answer true.
corrections.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp|DirectX9Renderer.cpp}}'s CreateEffectRenderer compiles the caller's HLSL (SM2/SM3) into a D3D9EffectRenderer, and {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp|D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp}} binds it for SpriteBatch, so there the source does determine the pixels. DirectX9Renderer does not override ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT(), so it answers false and the capability profile states that ShaderEffect source does not determine rendered pixels on this renderer, which under-claims the SpriteBatch route. For 3D, ShaderEffect::FillGpuDrawParams sets only customEffectRequested and customEffectRenderer, which {{src:modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9EffectDraw.cpp|D3D9EffectDraw.cpp}}'s DrawPrimitivesExImpl never reads. With the remaining GpuDrawParams defaults (vertex colour on, texture and lighting off) the cascade reaches DrawBasicEffectEXT, which draws a 16-byte (VertexPositionColor) stream with the stock vertex-colour shader and throws std::runtime_error (“(BasicEffect): stride N … has no matching CNA vertex layout”) for every other stride. Neither outcome names the unsupported custom effect.
corrections.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed. Read: DirectX9Renderer::CreateEffectRenderer, the SpriteBatch custom-effect flush in D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp, DirectX9Renderer::DrawPrimitivesExImpl and DrawBasicEffectEXT, ShaderEffect::FillGpuDrawParams in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/ShaderEffect.cpp|ShaderEffect.cpp}}, the GpuDrawParams defaults and the ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT contract in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}}, and GraphicsDevice::BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}. The DIRECTX9 ShaderEffect work item (plans/plan_dx9.md, D9-112) scoped the feature to SpriteBatch::Begin(effect). Because the false answer and the profile text warn callers that source does not drive pixels, the 3D fallback itself is inside CNA's documented capability contract; what remains is the inconsistent, misleadingly named failure on the 3D route and the SpriteBatch under-claim. XNA games use compiled effects, which DIRECTX9 supports separately; ShaderEffect is a CNA extension.
corrections.regression_test: A DIRECTX9 fixture that draws one VertexPositionColor and one VertexPositionTexture triangle with a ShaderEffect and asserts either the shader's constant colour for both (if 3D execution is implemented) or the same named NotSupportedException for both; plus a capability test that pins what ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() answers against the routes it describes.
corrections.blast_radius: Engine or game code that uses ShaderEffect for 3D on DIRECTX9 without checking ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT(): 16-byte vertex streams draw with wrong pixels and no error, and other layouts fail with an error that points at BasicEffect rather than the custom effect. Code that consults the capability profile is told source never drives pixels and may give up SpriteBatch custom effects that do work. SpriteBatch custom effects themselves and compiled XNA effects are unaffected.
corrections.workaround: Use compiled effects for 3D on DIRECTX9, and use ShaderEffect there only through SpriteBatch::Begin.

verdicts.note: Borderline REFUTED for the headline claim (CustomEffects is defined as acceptance only); kept as a narrower low-severity bug for the inconsistent 3D refusal and the SpriteBatch under-claim.

corrections.blast_radius: The direct effect at 009d40f5 is narrow. No in-tree GL renderer requests multisampling or a channel layout through GlContextDescription: EasyGL's RequestedGlContext and OpenGL4's RequestedContext ask only for a version and profile, a 24-bit depth buffer, an 8-bit stencil buffer and double buffering, which DescribeFormat honours. Nothing in the tree reads GetContextAttributes outside tests (PlatformGlContextOwner::GetAttributes has no caller). The in-tree consequence is the legacy fallback: on a driver without, or refusing, wglCreateContextAttribsARB, an EasyGL or OpenGL4 renderer that asked for a 3.3 Core context silently receives the legacy bootstrap context and nothing at context creation reports the downgrade. Out-of-tree renderers or tools built on the platform service get the requested description back instead of the granted one.

verdicts.note: Contract violation confirmed; severity lowered because no in-tree consumer requests the ignored fields or reads the misreported attributes.
